prompt: State the fundamental theorem of calculus and say why it is true.
answer: If f is continuous and F(x) is the integral of f from a to x, then F'(x) = f(x); so the integral from a to b equals G(b) - G(a) for any antiderivative G. The reason: adding a thin strip from x to x + h adds about f(x) h of area, so the area grows at rate f(x).
